gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-atkinson-hyper: Precise and a bit stubborn, Blockletter holds its pencil-line outlines at zero modulation while Atkinson Hyperlegible adds only a faint stroke variation beneath. That shared restraint is the glue.
Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono reads like a plain sans with its spacing stretched wide, each counter breathing out. Blockletter, by contrast, is the one with wire-cut strokes and a bold display attitude.

Blockletter takes the top spot with a squat, brush-pen belly and outlines like steel cable, no thick-thin shift anywhere. And Atkinson Hyperlegible Next supplies the opposite pleasure: big-eyed lowercase and unlatched rounds that stay easy to follow.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-biryani: Chunky, tall-bellied and unshaded, Blockletter sets a precise tone up top. And Biryani, a sans-serif with wide-eyed e shapes, is happiest when the heading is sized well above it.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-blinker: A squat, brush-pen belly gives Blockletter its look, with every line drawn at the same pencil pressure. Blinker is a plain sans whose lowercase fills most of the height, so shrinking the heading would flatten the gap between them.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-carrois-gothic: Carrois Gothic is the quiet one here, a sans-serif with a high-set x-height and generous openings. Under Blockletter's pressure-free pen and squat belly, a long page of it would read smoothly and without fuss.
Blockletter's ruler-drawn, constant-width line and squat brush-pen belly make it unmistakable next to Carrois Gothic SC. Its sans partner stays modest, with open curve endings.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-chocolate-clas: Blunt, tall-bellied and entirely free of thick-and-thin shifts, Blockletter leads with a precise pencil line. Chocolate Classical Sans follows in a sans with a big lowercase and a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, easy across a long stretch.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-comme: Blockletter's lines never grow heavier on the downstrokes, and its squat, brush-pen belly gives the heading a precise, drawn look. Comme answers in a smooth sans.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-cossette-texte: Blockletter opens with a pencil-drawn, squat-bellied heading. Cossette Texte, a sans with a prominent x-height and wide-eyed e, tends to look best when the heading is given generous size over it.
